name: Copperveil Intelligence
full_legal_name: Copperveil Intelligence Systems Corponation, Sovereign Data Enterprise
sovereign_territory: Veil Campus — a 6-square-kilometer fortified data complex in the former suburb of Warren, Michigan, plus legally recognized sovereign data jurisdiction over all information processed through Copperveil's sensor networks regardless of physical location. This 'data sovereignty' doctrine is contested by seven other corponations and has not been fully adjudicated by the Meridian Compact.
founding_story: Copperveil was assembled in 2140 from the intellectual property assets of four bankrupt smart-city contractors, purchased at liquidation by venture capital firm Herongate Partners. The resulting entity held patents on predictive crowd-flow modeling, behavioral anomaly detection, and passive biometric identification across a combined sensor network of roughly 2.4 million nodes already embedded in GLMZ infrastructure from the contractors' previous municipal contracts. Herongate installed Tomas Severyn — a former Eastern European intelligence community consultant — as founding CEO and took the corponation public in 2143. Severyn remains in the role, and Herongate retains a 28% stake.
security_force: The Copper Watch — 1,100 personnel focused almost entirely on cyber-defense, counter-intrusion, and the physical protection of sensor node infrastructure. The Copper Watch maintains a dedicated 200-person rapid response team for what internal documentation calls 'data integrity events,' which external observers interpret as meaning situations where someone has obtained Copperveil data without authorization and needs to be located.
key_detail: Copperveil's ARGUS predictive system has a documented 94.7% accuracy rate for anticipating civil unrest events more than 72 hours before they occur. The corponation sells ARGUS access to 34 corponation security forces and 11 Compact-recognized municipal authorities. It does not publicly disclose which ones.
relationship_to_big_20: Not a Big 20 member. The Big 20 collectively declined Copperveil's application for membership in 2147 in a rare unanimous vote, almost certainly because full membership would require Copperveil to submit to Compact financial disclosure standards that would reveal which Big 20 members are paying for what surveillance products. Copperveil filed a formal protest and then quietly continued selling to Big 20 members at premium rates.
full_text: Copperveil Intelligence Systems is the entity that knows where you were, predicts where you will go, and has already sold that information to at least one organization with an interest in your behavior before you have made your morning coffee. It is not the only surveillance corponation in GLMZ, but it is the largest, the oldest in the current form, and the most deeply integrated into the physical infrastructure of the corridor. Its 2.4 million passive sensor nodes — embedded in transit systems, building facades, street furniture, and utility infrastructure during the smart-city boom of the 2030s — form the most comprehensive civilian monitoring network in the Great Lakes region. Copperveil does not describe itself as a surveillance company. Its marketing materials use the phrase 'predictive safety infrastructure,' and its sales teams emphasize the ARGUS system's role in preventing industrial accidents, optimizing emergency response, and reducing corponation security costs. These claims are all technically accurate. They are also not the reason ARGUS subscriptions are priced at Φ40 million annually for enterprise tier access. Tomas Severyn is a famously private figure who gives approximately one public interview per year, always in controlled settings, always focused on infrastructure efficiency rather than the nature of what Copperveil actually does. Inside the corponation, there is a cultural emphasis on the word 'clarity' — clarity of data, clarity of purpose, clarity of process. Employees describe a workplace that is unusually quiet, unusually orderly, and unusual in its insistence that what they do is a public good. The Compact's ongoing deliberation over Copperveil's 'data sovereignty' doctrine is widely considered one of the most consequential unresolved legal questions in GLMZ, because if upheld, it would give Copperveil effective jurisdictional authority over information generated anywhere in the corridor.

glmzTerritory.description: The Veil Campus — fortified intelligence and behavioral analysis complex in the Evanston buffer zone of Zone 3. Sells corponation intelligence to other corponations; their neutral-zone position between Zone 1-2 power centers and Zone 4+ infrastructure allows independent operation without becoming a client of any single power.
glmzTerritory.grayZoneRelationship: Pays premium rates for intelligence sourced from Gray Zone networks. Their most reliable assets are people the corponations do not bother to watch.
